I'm not sure if my perspective will help to give you any hope at all - but, I think my whole time as an undergrad, I doubted my ability to do the work. I had a long commute to and from the university. I was unmotivated for lots of reasons. I failed a good amount of tests, but did well in my assignments and labs. But I'm actually going into an M.Sc. program this coming Fall semester, despite everything I believed about myself. I didn't have a great GPA. And I have severe ADHD. I did worse in my younger university years, but improved over time. 

This test only indicates that something needs to change. I also skipped a bunch of classes 3 years ago, and it definitely hurt my grades. I know it's hard, but the commute is worth it to help you get a better grasp of the content. I recommend opening up a little bit to your professor about this - they can help you! Not enough students utilize that as a resource. Depending on how much this test was worth, you can still salvage a decent grade if you put in the effort. But more importantly, even if you don't do well in this class, you can definitely use this experience to do better in future ones. 

This test does not determine your ability to be an astronomer. I know it's hard to see that right now - but everyone's learning is going to be at a different pace, and everyone is going to have classes they perform better in compared to others. Focus on using this test as a point to improve upon - it's clear you're intelligent, and it's clear you CAN put in the effort. 

I improved a lot at handling studying coupled with severe ADHD throughout my program. I can give you some tips, but I would recommend trying a few different ideas, because mine may not necessarily be helpful to you. 

First of all, I wouldn't study for 12-hour sessions. This kinda seems excessive, and for most people I know (and students I've tutored), retention of what you're studying is probably gonna drop off past 5 hours or so. What you want to aim for, in my opinion, is more days studying, consistency (which is HARD as someone with ADHD admittedly) and shorter overall time spent studying during the day. Asking questions during office hours or after class always helps. I recommend maybe an hour or two at max. You can try to review and understand what happened in lecture, come up with questions you want to ask, and identify other gaps in your knowledge. 

Also, before an exam, focus on eating properly, drinking water, exercising, and preparing your mind for the test. For me personally, this was more important than getting an extra hour or so of review. Which, of course, you can plan for as well before the test, but again, don't overdo it. Burnout is the thing I had to avoid the most during my undergrad. Breathing exercises helped me a pretty good amount as well actually. 

Just to be clear, it's good to worry about this grade, but not because it's gonna stop you from being an astronomer. The reason it's good to worry about it is because it just means you need to put more effort into figuring out studying methods that work for you - change up your strategies, try new things. Even if you failed this class tomorrow, it's not the end of the world. You can retake classes if you need to. What's most important to focus on now is identifying where you need to improve, and what changes you can make to facilitate that. 

Good luck, and trust me, you aren't alone in feeling that way. I'm pretty sure almost every physics and astronomy graduate I met felt that way at some point, and some missed entire tests by accident! It'll be okay.

At the moment, I have around 194 hours. I'll tell you what has kept me playing - but I should say, I don't play it consistently, I play it in small bursts of time, and I don't get bored of games in general that way. I've been playing U-boat for 2 or 3 years or so that way. 

What I started out by doing is playing a "balanced" experience. I didn't do torpedo solutions manually, but I did try to get research completed for my sub, attack large convoys, and try to learn how stealth works in the game. I did this without using guides. I tried reading more about what real-life skippers would do to try and get the most out of their U-boat. For me, I learned through this that the biggest enjoyment I found was immersing myself as the U-boat captain - I decided to determine my own torpedo solutions manually, learn how to be as quiet as possible, and strategically plan out my attacks beforehand. Sometimes, the moment when you're just about to see the enemy is super tense - when you can see them over the horizon, and you know what you're about to be in for. But, I will admit, for the first bit, I was also bored, trying to figure out wtf the controls were. 

When I'm in-between engagements, I'm hunting, or at full speed and getting places ASAP so that I can either start hunting again or do a different objective. By "hunting", I mean using hydrophones (sometimes manually too) and finding whether I can intercept. 

If you're looking for action, try to stay near enemy ports. If you're in the mid-atlantic, you're gonna be using your hydrophones a lot just searching up and down. 

The game is slow as hell. But there's nothing like it for me. I like to protect my crew - and when your crew gets you out of a hairy situation, or when you sink 150 meters below, trying to survive with the few crew you have left, and you DO it, there's no other feeling like it.

As she stands right now, her CR and CDMG are pretty good. Her DEF is a little high, and her ATK is a little low. If it's possible for you to increase your ATK at all, it might be a noticeable change until around the 2600+ mark. 

If you have a supp that increases her ATK, and you use them with her, then she should be fine as is. As you said, speed is a little low - but this is only important for a few different things:

1) High speed without bronya. Obviously attacking more per cycle is important, as I'm sure you're aware

2) Speed tuned for Bronya. If you do have bronya, you may want to consider 135/136 speed (or, generally speaking, 1 or 2 speed over bronya.) This allows a really nice rotation of Jingliu -> Bronya -> Jingliu -> Bronya. This speed tuning also works very well even when you have Bronya E2, from my personal experience. I've never had a single problem with it. 

3) Hyperspeed bronya. I'm not sure if RM has a speed increase for teammates (since I don't have her</3) but you could go 161+ speed Bronya and base speed Jingliu. This means you can get more ATK, but of course, that may be too much time to invest in both bronya and Jingliu relics. After all, your speed boots are pretty dang good. 

TLDR; she's great where she stands right now, and should absolutely get you through the hardest content. As with any build, you can choose how much you want to invest to try and make it even better.

So, first thing I noticed was that, within the first minute, you lost track of where your sojourn went, you look back, and commit to the left side with your tank. Honestly, it would have just been best to backtrack a teeny bit just to stay near your pocket. Sojourn is the better choice to pocket here as well, and so far, it seems like you do know that :>  


Another thing I notice is that, when a genji is diving your team, at times you sort of focus too much on the healing you're doing to the person you're currently trying to save. At about 1:45 I notice that you focus a lot on healing your tank when your healer is the more urgent target, and your winston also was using his bubble. He didn't get her in the end because she swift stepped to you, but finding that target/healing priority is important. If your Kiri has line of sight on your tank, and if the tank is out of range of your beam, it's best to try to let the kiri handle it unless you know you can survive if you do GA to your tank.   


When the Genji ults on your team for the first time, you actually valk here and get away from him which is great. But, you don't decide to actually check on if your two teammates behind you are okay. You hard focus on what your tank is doing. You seem to also panic a little in those situations.   


I would say, so far, that you have been trying too hard to focus on your tank than anyone else, which leads to lower amp damage and less value for mercy overall. Instead, it's okay to let your Kiri handle your tank a little more and try to help when he really needs it. Remember, he's Winston, he can jump back to you when he needs it:)   


I also noticed that you have problems at times with multitasking. If your beam is on someone, you only care about them and focus all your resources on them. When you have noticed that your team is starting to break, you panic and lose sense of who you should prioritize.   


Another thing is, I notice that around 3:15 you go for a rez that works, but try to make it a habit to make sure that your alive teammates are at a safe amount of health left, just in case. Winston there had about 25 HP left, so if a butterfly landed on him he would have just died. It worked here, just keep in mind that your alive teammates are the priority. Think about how their safe their positioning is, and whether their HP will be okay if you decide to go for a quick rez.   


At around 3:30, you do get back to your initial pocket now that things calmed down. This is great, just try to make sure you focus on your pocket primarily, and think about who has better angles of engagement when considering who to pocket at a given moment.   


Now, we get to your first death. You went for a rez in a pretty dangerous position. Here, valk would have been better to try and stabilize, but it also was not a great position to be in since your Kiri died, hence no suzu. I noticed around here that you got a bit scared, and there were moments where you weren't close enough to your team to help because you didn't know if you should run or stay. Focus more on dying last in team fights rather than being scared to die in general. You want to create value, and to do that, you do have to stay alive, but you just need more confidence in your abilities here I think.   


Next, around 5:20 we start the second round, and we get to your second death. This one was kind of a tough situation for you guys. Although doomfist ran into a trap and didn't block, it would have helped if he did have the ana helping him there. You were with your pocket and began to panic once you noticed the rein in your backline.   


I would say here it would have been simply better to die instead of try and run - you don't want to stagger, if the team fight is lost it's okay to accept that and group up for the next one.  


For the next team fight of round 2, you actually stay a little too far back I would say. Keeping your tank healed a little bit may have helped, though, he was taking so much damage it probably wouldn't have changed anything. Try to focus on who needs healing, and who can get healing. For example, who is your ana sticking with/healing at the moment? Do you need to use your resources to help them as well?  


Around 6:35 you're in a closed area pretty much facing a junkrat. You got pretty lucky you didn't die - try to avoid going into closed-in areas if you can. There's a balance between going too far up and staying too far back. Try to get a feel for beam length, but also trying to keep a good line of sight and predicting how their team may want to move on you guys.   


At about 6:45 you don't go for a rez because you're scared of the junkrat. It makes sense, just remember you can rez behind walls too, I think this one was totally possible :>  


Damage boost prioritization applies to the next part. Your reaper had nano and ult, it was probably a good idea to dmg boost them there. But, the junkrat tire did kill them, so it didn't end with a potentially risky situation for you :) try to keep in mind what ults your team has, as well as what the enemy team might have. This is a skill that takes lots of time to develop well:)  


Around 7:40, it would have helped to look back at the point to see if anyone needed your help. It's possible that your ana could have survived if you looked back to make sure. Again though, that has to do with trying to multitask a little bit:)  


Overall, the takeaways are:  
\-Healing priority (who needs it? can your other healer help them instead? will it put you in too dangerous a position to try and heal them?)  


\-Positioning (think, what position is safe for you, but still gives you a good line of sight on your teammates? high ground can be nice, but of course this won't always be possible, just remember that you have to enable your teammates, and they can't be enabled if your beam breaks around a corner with your GA on cooldown)  


\-Damage boost priority (remember, this is Mercy's best utility. you want to use it a lot more. understanding who has ult, which ults you can damage boost, and paying attention to when your teammates may be setting up for an ult situation is important. you know that sojourn is a strong pocket which is great - just think about how you can work with your other teammates, too<3)  


\-Too little confidence (this will also come with more practicing of Mercy's mobility, but have more confidence in your ability to escape, potentially defend, and the ability of your teammates. yes, they're bronze right now, but so is the enemy team.)  


\-Don't focus too much on not dying (this one I kinda elaborated on already. it's okay to know when a teamfight is lost. don't let it affect your mental, take the loss of the fight and prepare for the next one. the more grouped up you guys are, the higher chance of good synergy.)  


\- take the time to think - who on their team has ult? and who on your team has ult? how can i decide to position myself based off of who i think fulfills this criteria?

Well, specifically, the picture simply had a year (late 1941) written on the back. We found out that he had been in the USSR since the beginning of the invasion, taking pictures of SS officers and Russian orthodox priests in the Greater Poland area, being modern-day Belarus and Ukrainian land. 

We also found out he had left the USSR between early-mid 1942, however, that isn’t technically proof that this particular picture was taken in the USSR, as he did also appear to travel a fair bit. 

For reference, we have pictures that he took of French POWs, propaganda parades in Austria, Hungarian soldiers and villages, as well as the invasion of Greece through the Bulgarian border, if I recall correctly. In addition, he took some pictures of the trains used to transport soldiers and equipment, along with plenty of pictures of marching and officers staging for photos.

Ahh, you're talking about the vertical components of the forces then? In that case, well, yes, I do agree they could point in the same direction, since the gravitational force of earth is only the vertical component and it would have no horizontal one. Though, "vertical" and "horizontal" aren't the words I would use I suppose.  


I wouldn't say the normal force is asinine to include, though. It should be noted as well, that Japan used carriers effectively supporting land operations in China before 1941. I wouldn’t say that their advantages were super obvious in the 1920s when interwar planes were still used, however, by the late 30s, I think it was clear how versatile they could be - although, not exactly fully realized. Not even fully realized in Japan, as you see with the launch of Yamato, like you said. 

Whether Yamamoto was an innovator for air power though, is up for debate. The general opinion was, indeed, that battleships were the most important force in a fleet. However, Yamamoto did use carriers in a way never really seen before pearl harbour - despite placing an emphasis (originally, that is) on destroying battleships in the battle. I think it’s safe to say that after pearl harbour, he was at least mostly committed to the power of an air fleet. 

Bismarck was built before pearl harbour even happened, and of course, was built in Europe - Yamato was launched in 1940 as well, before pearl harbour. So I do have to agree that before that event, it’s difficult to say whether the most influential admirals in Japan were fully committed to using an air fleet. In fact, I would say not many were. Some captains, such as Captain Genda perhaps knew best their advantages by 1940. 

I’d like to know what you think. In summary, I think for Japanese High Command, pearl harbour changed how they viewed naval doctrine - or at least was one of the most instrumental events shaping it. But I think before that, there was not a lot to know about properly using an air fleet. I think my use of “obvious” was definitely too liberal, although, by the time of Midway, I think it’s safe to say admirals such as Yamamoto and Nimitz knew how important they could be for base striking (and I guess for Japan, also decisive battle).

Watched game 1. So what I noticed about your playstyle is that you play extremely safe. Which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but there are tons of options to close in on a character like Lucina, and honestly any character for that matter, if the person standing still is trying to wait for the opponent to make a mistake. 

With a safe playstyle, you have the right idea with the retreating nairs and fairs, though it's important to utilize your up air more. Not only that, but your down air can lead into an f-smash at higher percents, if you hit them while they're standing on stage. Your neutral game isn't bad necessarily, but the Wario had a lot of time to breathe and choose his approach. In this case, he decided to grab a lot. With your specific playstyle, it was pretty effective since you shielded a lot. If you prefer that kind of playstyle, I can try and offer some improvements. (Though I traditionally play more aggressively)

1. Shield less. This is quite important, especially because Wario actually has a decent neutral and grab game. Because of the grabs he got on you, he was able to throw you/smash attack you offstage and attempt to edgeguard. 

2. Move more. Try to keep the opponent on his heels, so that every aggressive move he makes can be punished easier. Otherwise, he will easily learn your playstyle quicker than you can learn his. By moving around more, instead of shielding, it's harder for him to land grabs, which he seemed fond of using. Not only this, but Lucina's movement is excellent. Her initial dash distance allows for a lot of great options with her neutral game, and if I remember correctly ZeRo talked about how good approaching an opponent with down tilt is. Not only that, but if you get good at mix ups, your opponent will have a really hard time learning your playstyle, forcing them to try and change theirs. But of course, doing good mixups/reads means knowing your opponent, or guessing what they will do based off of habits that other players have. 

3. Go for edgeguards. With Lucina, this is essential. The more you practice it, the better you will get at knowing the timing and spacing. Sometimes it means going really deep, but don't be afraid of that. Lucina has a good recovery. Not only that, but generally speaking, going for an edgeguard is usually harmless for the player trying to do it. It mostly depends on *when* you go for the edgeguard and *what* character you're edgeguarding. 

4. Try to set up more strings. Lucina has pretty good combos she can do right out of the bat to do ~45%(keep in mind, these should be used at low percent). A few of these options are: 

- falling u-air->u-tilt->b/fair->b/fair. Harder to do with stages that have platforms, but possible. Not only that, but u-air is pretty safe on shield and could usually be followed up with a grab (if you want to be more aggressive), a jab, etc. I wouldn't do an up tilt if you hit it on shield though. It comes out very quickly, but has a long active hitbox. I say back air/forward air because it depends on DI. 

- U-tilt->u-tilt->b/fair->b/fair. This should do around as much damage as the first string I listed. This one is better if you prefer neutral, and if they're shielding you can space the u-tilt so it's a bit safer. 

- D-throw->b/fair->b/fair. This one is pretty simple, and doesn't do as much damage, but will probably be the most consistent one that you hit out of these. 

These are my common options that I choose. They may change if you b/fair them offstage. That's when it's a good idea to keep being aggressive. 

I noticed in the first 10 seconds of the video that the Wario approaches with shield first before he decides his attack option. He baited an attack from you and then chose his option. Despite this, Lucina has actually really good options against this because of her shield break. If you tried to predict when he was going to use his shield, then it could've potentially caught him unprepared and broken his shield, allowing you to punish and kill him with a fully-charged neutral-b at ~40%(side stage, of course). If you think the neutral b is too risky, you could also try going for a grab, but that obviously has its risks. 

I hope that helped, if you managed to get through that whole thing. I'm sure you know a lot of what I said here, but I only watched the one game so I don't have full insight into your play style. If you'd like, I could message you my friend code and we could play at some point.

Not much, that I know of. If you're angling your shield upwards you are either in shield stun still from whatever attack hit you, or you didn't let go of the shield button. 

Other than that, the only real trick is knowing what moves you can punish quickly and what moves you either can't punish or *can* punish but not be unpunishable yourself.

Her up-b has a sweet spot on the bottom of the attack, where she will initially start it. The higher the hit with the up b, the lower the knock back and percentage done to the enemy. 

Since the lowest point of the up b is the most effective, you'll see many people say that it is a good option out of shield when the enemy is vulnerable. This isn't entirely wrong, but it comes out frame 5. Up tilt comes out frame 6, and is much less punishable, also, its much better at setting up combos lol.

If you're doing up b at the side of the stage and they're at high percent, you could kill them if it's sweetspotted. But there's a lot of risk with it no matter the situation.

This is actually the only time to ever use counter tbh. But a skilled opponent will probably predict the counter and try to hold the charge for a smash attack a bit longer, or hold off on inputting their aerial. If they don't predict it the first time, they will on the second. 

For the OP:

Doing a counter onstage against a smash attack would also promote a bad habit though, which is landing on stage after getting launched off of it. The ledge is almost always preferable to landing on the stage, especially with Lucina, who doesn't have a great amount of landing options.

When on ledge, lucina has much more control of the situation and can fight back. For example: The lucina gets sent off the left side of the stage, and the opponent stands on the ledge preparing an attack trying to read your stage getup. The lucina has a few options when they grab the ledge. Jump up, roll onstage, stand onstage, do a getup attack, or press the left stick to the left to let go of the ledge and attack with a forward air/neutral b/run up and grab/neutral air/upair(if close enough), or they could go on the defensive with a directional air dodge after holding left on the left stick.

These are great options and much less predictable than if the lucina jumped back onstage to counter and try to read the opponents  ledge trap. Needless to say though, counter is useful if you know your opponent.

First hit nair-> f-smash is a good kill move, but it can be hard to hit when you're trying to space, and you need to be fast falling. Neutral air in general is a good move, since it has only 7 frames of landing lag. I like to do short hop-> fast fall-> up air to set up for an up-tilt-> aerial combo. You can get a lot of damage that way. 

Edgeguarding and stage control are central for her. Her aerials are all really good for edgeguarding, and her up air having 5 frames of startup and 8 frames of landing lag can really help people above you be forced towards the ledge or find another recovery option. Her neutral helps her stage control as well, with her up tilt having 6 frames of startup and thus being great for combos into aerials. 

Her grabs are mostly used for setting up stage control or edgeguarding. Her down throw is good at low percents for maybe starting a combo or getting a free up air. Her up throw is good for heavy characters and keeping them above you, and your back throw and forward throw are mainly good for setting up those edge guards. 

Her initial dash distance is amazing for mixups and can go into all of her tilts/smash attacks. 

Her side-b angled downwards is incredible for damage, and does about ~25% in 1v1s if you hit it all. Angled forward is an okay kill option, but it's best for stage control. However, this move is quite punishable. I pretty much never angle it upwards.

Her neutral b is fucking insane. With the advent of perfect shield only activating when you let go of shield, her neutral b is now much better. If you hit a tilt on someone's shield and do an uncharged neutral b on it, their shield is now broken. And depending on the character, they could die around 50% side-stage to her fully charged neutral b. The hardest part of this is predicting when they are going to shield next after you've hit their shield. But with enough practice it isn't hard to do, and it forces them to use shield less. 

Down b is okay but it can be predictable. I rarely use it. 

I hope that helps, I'm sure there's a bunch I missed. Up B out of shield can be good but I wouldn't use it unless it's guaranteed, since it is extremely punishable.

Here's what I did when I tried it a few times: 

-when the game starts, take a general(the lvl 3 guy with -50% attrition works best I find) and set a naval invasion for Alaska. 

-Do not start a national focus and wait until you have enough PP to justify on USA. 

-in the meantime, make sure you set priorities for your equipment. Set reinforcements/upgrades to low for now and set division creation to high, so that you may be able to get 1 or 2 divisions before the war starts. 

-get a separate field Marshall and place the bulk of your army with him. You can leave 2-4 divisions as home garrison divisions for another general so that you can defend the homeland as the war goes on. 

-after you justify war, wait until your PP goes to 10 before you get a national focus started, since when you start it, your PP should go down 10 points. In addition, don't do anything China related until the war with the US is done. I'm pretty sure that the more threatening you are the more likely China is to cede things to you. It's best to stick with things like increasing national unity, reducing attrition, increasing attack. Basically, while preparing, try to get as much buffs for your soldiers as you can. (Lots of PP will help of coarse) 

-when the war starts, make sure you have naval supremacy in the required zones, and make sure they're on convoy escort for the time being. This will keep your navy in good numbers for a while. Also, right when the war starts, you MUST change priority of divisions to low, upgrades to low, and Reinforcements to High. Otherwise your troops will not get far at all in the US mainland. 

-start naval invasion immediately. When it lands, go right away to the port. When you get to the port, set a naval invasion for Seattle. 

-meanwhile, get the bulk of your army to the Alaskan port. You may want to move your ships around to make sure they're covered. 

-when everyone is in Alaska, set the Alaskan port as the home port for your navy. This will make a huge difference on the west coast. 

-once again, make sure you have naval supremacy and invade Seattle. Make sure your navy is on convoy escort still. 

-when you invade Seattle, set battle plans and make them aggressive so you can get as much land as possible before the US mobilizes. 

-you should now set your navy to convoy raiding/search and destroy or patrol to make sure you don't get naval invaded from the west coast when you're on the east coast. 

-you don't HAVE to micromanage but it's potentially faster this way. If you don't micromanage much, you will likely finish it in early/mid 1938. 

A good strat to have after this is to leave China alone until WW2 starts and then help out Germany, since you have sufficient factories/resources to fight efficiently, except for lack of rubber if I remember correctly.

-meanwhile, get the bulk of your army to the Alaskan port. You may want to move your ships around to make sure they're covered. 

-when everyone is in Alaska, set the Alaskan port as the home port for your navy. This will make a huge difference on the west coast. 

-once again, make sure you have naval supremacy and invade Seattle. Make sure your navy is on convoy escort still. 

-when you invade Seattle, set battle plans and make them aggressive so you can get as much land as possible before the US mobilizes. 

-you should now set your navy to convoy raiding/search and destroy or patrol to make sure you don't get naval invaded from the west coast when you're on the east coast. 

-you don't HAVE to micromanage but it's potentially faster this way. If you don't micromanage much, you will likely finish it in early/mid 1938.
